keyTerms.definition: Which sources each lesson concept comes from.
Locally authored prerequisite content, not instructor lectures.

recall.question: What do the playlist titles name?
recall.answer: Topics only: not leaf items, definitions, or numbers.

keyTerms.definition: Risk, loss selection, consistency, bias and variance, penalties, priors, splits, CV, capacity, curves, leakage, shift.
A skill the learner can show after the lesson.

recall.question: What must a learner be able to do after this lesson?
recall.answer: Write empirical and population risk, defend a loss choice, decompose one MSE, run ridge and MAP, run k-fold CV without leakage, read learning curves, name three leak channels, quantify one covariate shift.

keyTerms.definition: Question, toy, rule, computed example, code, checks, costs, alternatives, failure case.
Russian-doll ladder positions 0-10 marking each step.

recall.question: What does each section open with?
recall.answer: A concrete question, then a toy built from zero.

keyTerms.definition: R_hat: the scoreboard after the game you played.
R: the scoreboard you would get playing forever.
Empirical risk minimization: picks the best-scoring rule from the sample.

recall.question: What did R_hat and R come out to on the toy?
recall.answer: Both 0.25: they agree by luck of the toy, not by law.

recall.question: Why is a memorizer a counterexample?
recall.answer: R_hat = 0 but R = 0.5: the scoreboard lied.

keyTerms.definition: The price list you hand to the optimizer.
Prices large errors quadratically; buys the mean.
A smooth stand-in (hinge, logistic) for the non-smooth 0-1 loss.

recall.question: What does each loss buy on y=[0,1,1]?
recall.answer: Squared buys the mean 2/3 with risk 2/9. Absolute buys the median. 0-1 buys the majority class.

recall.question: Why does squared loss fail for classification?
recall.answer: It punishes confident correct answers, e.g. predicting 3 for label 1 pays 4.

keyTerms.definition: A contract: IID sampling, a fixed estimator, n to infinity.
Independent, identically distributed draws from a fixed distribution.

recall.question: Why did the dependent flips quadruple the MSE?
recall.answer: The sample of 4 carried one flip of information: 0.21 vs 0.0525.

recall.question: When does the contract fail in practice?
recall.answer: Feedback loops: the model changes user behavior, so the distribution moves with the model.

keyTerms.definition: How far the average estimate sits from truth.
How much the estimate wobbles across datasets.
bias squared plus variance plus irreducible noise.

recall.question: How did the Laplace estimator beat the MLE?
recall.answer: MSE 0.02778 vs 0.0525: it traded a little bias for a lot less wobble.

recall.question: Why does the split fail for 0-1 loss?
recall.answer: No clean additive split exists; 0-1 error is not bias squared plus variance plus noise.

keyTerms.definition: A tax on bigness added to the training objective.
The tax rate: 0 is the old problem, huge pins w at 0.
The penalized least-squares solution, here w = 13/16 = 0.8125.

recall.question: What did the penalty do to the toy?
recall.answer: w moved 0.9286 to 0.8125; the penalized objective fell 3.6531 to 3.4375.

recall.question: Why can a penalty misfire?
recall.answer: On unstandardized features it punishes units, not weights.

keyTerms.definition: A belief about w before the data.
Maximizes belief times fit; here w = 0.8125.
The log prior is the penalty: same move in two languages.

recall.question: Show the ridge-MAP equivalence on the toy.
recall.answer: Gaussian prior N(0,0.5) gives w_MAP = 13/16 = 0.8125, exactly the C05 ridge answer.

recall.question: When does a prior hurt?
recall.answer: tau squared = 0.001 pins w near 0 no matter what the points say.

keyTerms.definition: Fit on one part, score on a part the model never saw.
The model is frozen before scoring on the test part.

recall.question: What were the honest and optimistic numbers?
recall.answer: Train MSE 0.4821 optimistic; test MSE 0.8653 honest. Gap 0.3832.

recall.question: What does the C07 split not guard?
recall.answer: The wrong future: a test set drawn from the training distribution.

keyTerms.definition: The split idea run in a circle: every point gets one turn as the test stand-in.
k-fold with k = n: fit on n-1, score the held-out one.

recall.question: What did CV pick on the toy?
recall.answer: lambda = 0.5: the penalty wins on points it did not train on.

recall.question: What is selection bias in CV?
recall.answer: Tuning on the CV score, then reporting the best CV score as the final number.

keyTerms.definition: How many different functions the model class can express.
Test error falls then explodes as capacity grows past the truth.

recall.question: What happened at degree 3?
recall.answer: Train MSE 0 exactly: 4 parameters for 4 points interpolate. Test MSE 28.5613.

recall.question: Why is capacity relative to data?
recall.answer: With n = 400 the degree-3 fit would be harmless: the U bottom moves right.

keyTerms.definition: Train and validation error plotted against n.
val minus train: a data-starvation signal.

recall.question: What did the gap do from n=3 to n=40?
recall.answer: Shrank 0.3084 to 0.1104: more data helps this problem.

recall.question: What does a plateau above the noise floor mean?
recall.answer: The model family is wrong: no n fixes it. That is the bias signal.

keyTerms.definition: Information from the future smuggled into training.
Build features only from information available at decision time.

recall.question: What did the 1.0 accuracy measure?
recall.answer: The leak, not the model: deployment falls to the 0.6 majority share.

recall.question: Name three subtle leak channels.
recall.answer: Full-data-mean imputation, feature selection on all data, early-stopping on the test set.

keyTerms.definition: The distribution of x moves.
The relation itself moves: no reweighting recovers it.

recall.question: Quantify the C12 shift.
recall.answer: Train MSE 0.0986 on x in [0,3]; shift-test MSE 0.5548 on x in [4,6].

recall.question: When can reweighting fix a shift?
recall.answer: Only when the shift is in x and the support overlaps.

keyTerms.definition: The file with worked answers, at lessons/u05/keys.md.
A question the learner answers; keys in lessons/u05/keys.md.

recall.question: Where are the answers to E01-E30?
recall.answer: In lessons/u05/keys.md.

keyTerms.definition: The rung that moves the idea to a new situation.
Define, toy, derive, debug, transfer.

recall.question: What does the L10 debug rung ask?
recall.answer: Validation plateaus above the noise floor: name two causes.

keyTerms.definition: An original PNG, opened and read on 2026-10-06.
Bias squared falls, variance rises; U minimum at degree 2.

recall.question: What does f04 carry?
recall.answer: Grouped fold bars with CV means 1.8515 and 1.1806 in the legend.

keyTerms.definition: R35-R44, U03 gradients, U04 likelihood/MAP.
Open research extensions: nested CV theory, double descent, shift detection.

recall.question: What sends a learner to prerequisites.md first?
recall.answer: A miss on R35-R44, U03 gradients, or U04 likelihood/MAP.
